name: application-environment-switcher
title: Environment Switcher
description: Trigger button showing the current deploy environment with a colored status dot, opening a dropdown listing every environment with its own dot and a checkmark on the active one.
useWhen: Switching context between Development, Staging, and Production (or similar deploy targets) in an admin or internal tool.
You want the current environment always visible via a colored indicator, not just discoverable inside a menu.
The set of environments is small and fixed, unlike an open-ended workspace or project switcher.
avoidWhen: You're switching between an open-ended, growing list of workspaces or recent items — use a recent/pinned switcher instead.
There's only one environment (e.g. a single-tenant app) — the control adds a decision point with no real choice behind it.
responsiveBehavior: The trigger and dropdown are fixed-width and anchored to the trigger's left edge; on narrow viewports the panel may need repositioning to avoid overflowing the viewport edge.
accessibility: The trigger carries aria-haspopup and aria-expanded reflecting open state; the panel closes on Escape or an outside click.
Each environment's status dot is paired with its visible name — color is never the only way an environment is identified.
The active environment is marked with a visible checkmark icon in addition to a background tint, so the current selection is clear without relying on color alone.

variants.title: Environment Switcher
variants.description: A Staging trigger with an amber dot, opening a dropdown listing Development (gray), Staging (amber, active with checkmark), and Production (emerald).
accessibility: Each row's environment name and colored dot both convey identity; the active row adds a checkmark rather than relying on tint alone.

variants.title: Environment Switcher (Dark)
variants.description: The same trigger and dropdown adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Status dot colors and the active-row tint remain distinguishable at dark-surface contrast.
